newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, July 21 - There were no surprises in PORLA's latest figures on palm production and stocks of palm oil, PK/PKO in June. Even the total disappearance figure came within our estimate. CPO production dropped marginally by 0.6 percent to 787,800 tonnes from 792,500 tonnes (revised) in May but up 9.2 percent when compared to June last year. For the 6 months ended June, production expanded 10.4 percent or 383,700 tonnes to 4.082 million tonnes. This exceeded our May 14 projection of 4.015 million tonnes. The crop and yields in Peninsular Malaysia were better than we expected.

End June stocks of palm oil rose 73,800 tonnes to 786,100 tonnes. This is slightly lower than our recent estimate of 795,000 tonnes but 56,000 tonnes higher than our May 14 projection of 730,000 tonnes. Field crop survey conducted last week indicated production growth would continue, albeit, at a slower pace. The seasonal rise in production would comfortably exceed increases in exports and result in a big buildup in stocks. Our projection of CPO production this year is revised upward to 8.9 million tonnes.
Production this month is tentatively estimated to increase 5 percent or around 40,000 tonnes.

Last week, CPO futures prices advanced 39-40 ringgit or 3.5 percent. All the gains were attributed to the weakening ringgit which fell 4.3 percent or 1,075 points to close at 2.6120 to the U.S. dollar last week following concerted speculative attacks. September CPO futures settled at 1,167 ringgit, up from 1,128 a week ago but down from 1,186 ringgit on June 18. September RBD olein was quoted at $527.5, unchanged for the week but down $2.5 from a month ago.
We view last week's CPO price gains as a temporary rebound to the preceding 3-weeks losses of 71-62 ringgit.

The world supply-demand fundamentals of palm oil and other oils/fats have not improved in recent weeks. In the case of palm oil, the Malaysian scenario points to an even larger build-up in stocks in the coming months as compared to projections made a month ago.
Despite continuing purchases of RBD olein by a leading CPO producer-refiner last week, we had detected no shift or unexpected strength in demand to be optimistic on the price outlook.
We are projecting end September stocks of palm oil to be well above the one-million tonne level, possibly to 1.06 million tonnes.

While the majority of Malaysian economists and bankers felt the country's economic fundamentals do not warrant the ringgit depreciating to above the 2.6 level, they were also of the opinion that interest rates, which rose markedly last week, would remain at relatively high levels in the next few months. Producers/refiners should thus consider reviewing their stock holding level policy.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
